text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The situation on the Lithuanian boarder is worse than expected and in some cases smuggling schemes have been organised by top officials, Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said in a cabinet meeting.
- The Foreign Ministry and the new European Affairs Ministry did not succeed yesterday in deciding how to share out their functions, which some see as being duplicated in some areas.
- The Economy Ministry faces three major problems: how to stimulate industry and business, how to cut debts for energy and how to decentralise the energy sector.

- Prosecutor's office again questioned 89-year-old Aleksandras Lileikis, stripped of U.S. citizenship as an alleged participant of the Holocaust in Lithuania. Prosecutors said they need two to three more questioning sessions before deciding whether to press charges or not.
- Police detained two women, a teacher of religion among them, who are suspected of being behind a spate of vanadalism of churches at the end of last year.
- Vagnorius assured that the litas will not be unpegged from the dollar until the memorandum with the IMF expires on September 1.
- The European Council reduced the membership fee to $200,000 from $350,000 for Lithuania after it recalculated the country's GDP.
- Preliminary data shows that the tax office collected 6.664 billion litas for the national budget in 1996.
- Lithuania commemorated the 74th anniversary of when Klaipeda region joined Lithuania on January 15, 1923.
- President's office suspects that parliament is avoiding co-operation.

- Ignalina nuclear power plant produced 11.3 billion kilowatt hours of electric energy in 1996. Some 67 percent of it was consumed in Lithuania and 33 percent exported, four percent to Russia in exchange for nuclear fuel, 13 percent to Latvia and 16 percent to Byelorussia.
